text.title: Regression Test First Bugfix Workflow Decision Tree

decision-tree.root-question: Does a test built from the alert payload's inputs reproduce the same failure on every run against the unfixed code?

branch.conclusion: Skip: a non-deterministic fault gets structured logging and a synthetic monitor on the symptom, not a regression test that will flake. Route to observability or QA.

branch.question: Does the SLA allow the red test to be committed and shown failing in CI before the fix ships?

branch.conclusion: Ship the smallest hotfix; create the record with `red_test` pending, a follow-up ticket due within 14 days, and keep the alert open until the test merges.

branch.question: Has CI shown the new test failing on a test-only commit, with the alert's exception or wrong output, before any production-code commit?

branch.conclusion: Commit the test alone first; wait for the failing CI run; only then start the fix commit. If the failure reason differs from the alert, fix the assertions until it matches.
Run the rest of the flow: minimal fix with assertions untouched, green CI run cited alongside the red one, review date at merge plus 90 days against the alert's regression status.

example.p: Sentry issue reproduces with `amount=0.0, locale=tr_TR` on every run; SLA 24h leaves room; test `tests/regression/test_checkout_zero_amount.py` committed alone at `a1b2c3d`, CI run 76 shows `ValidationError` matching the alert → conclusion run-the-checklist; fix PR #9981, 18 lines, CI run 77 green, review 2026-08-22.
